x: It seems to have been a foregone conclusion that Portsmouth A.C., with the help of Hyman and Tulloh (with or without shoes) would win this race.
Pirie was an easy winner for S.L.H. smashing previous course records set by Hyman and Foord by nearly a minute. Ken Miller was a good third, with Thresher 7th, Walker 8th and Shippen 10th.

This is the leg where the race can be won and lost, and names such as Hyman (who produced a fantastic new record - 34 seconds better than his own previous best), Wilkinson, Perry, North, Reed, Edmonds, Hogan and Foord appeared - enough to frighten the stoutest of hearts.
For besides the oppresive heat he also had to contend with Messrs. Pirie, Hyman, Eldon & Co. Pat ran, relatively, as well as anybody in the field to record 14:14, but was outside the first six.
Hyman (Ports) 17:32 3.Herring(B'Hth)/D.Cooke (Port) 17:39

Well the strongest club in the South decided to enter for the first time - yes, Portsmouth A.C, and they must be given full credit for their win, for they succeeded without the inseparable Hyman/Tulloh partnership, who were performing great feats in Belgrade.
Walker was fighting it out with Hyman, Tulloh and Wilkinson across a stretch of plough, when the sole of his spiked shoe tore away from its upper.
It was here that Hyman threw away his team's advantage by misjudging the time of the take over and being caught with his track-suit on.(It was raining at the time).
A mammoth total of 370 runners started, including 48 internationals. Tulloh was 4th, Turner 5th, Fowler 7th, Hyman 9th, Bullivant 12th, J.
Both were eliminated from their heats of the 2 miles event. Thresher was beaton by O'Riordan (Eire), Kidd (Canada), Jackson, Hyman and T.
Brother Gerry chased Hyman home in the '3' with 13:47.6 and Bill Kerr finished two places and 11.6 secs. behind. Trevor Hart ran a useful Steeplechase time of 9:47.8 to finish 4th.

Charlie Dabbs ran well on Stage 1 to finish 4th, 18 seconds down on the leader (Collins of Surrey AC), but on the next leg Hyman beat Geoff North in the run-in and, for a moment, both Portsmouth teams were ahead of us.

In the absence of his brother Gerry,unable to run because of a bad cold, Geoff North ran an excellent race to lead the Belgrave team and finish a very good 12th.(In front of Cooke,Hyman and Tulloh!!).

L.O'Hara and Trevor Hart ran very well to take third and fourth places (both in front of Hyman). This was a particularly good performance in view of the fact that both had run in the Southern 2 miles the evening before.

In their first 3 miles race John Cooke (Portsmouth) and Dominic Kelly (Derby) finished first in 14:35.4 (!) followed by Hyman (Portsmouth) 14:44.8 Gerry 14:52.7, Turner (Liverpool) 14:54;4 and Geoff. 15:06.

Gerry North was also in great form, taking nearly a minute off Hyman, and Belgrave to within 20 seconds of the lead. Despite the acquisition of Dai Davies the Welsh Champion, and fastest stage times by Wiggs and Ellis, our old rivals TVH could still only get within 47 seconds of us at the finish.
Laurie produced his usual reliable effort and a finishing burst that took him to 5th, 11 seconds behind Portsmouth's Hyman and 23 seconds ahead of T.V.H.'s Goodman.
With Johnstone and Tulloh to lead them and Hyman marshalling the remainder Pompey could well be the biggest threat unless.............. unless the holders North Staffs and Stone think otherwise.
Gerry Williams gained selection for the County team and finished an excellent 58th at Leicester, ahead of such runners as Hyman, Heatley and Bullivant.

Hyman had also run 20 secs faster to bring Pompey a little nearer but Coventry had another bad stage with Dowall clocking 30:29 in 10th place - 1:11 slower than Trevor and nearly 4 minutes behind the leaders, Birchfield.
Reading had now joined T.VH. as leading challengers whilst Portsmouth improved two places through Hyman. LEFT:Chris Steer sends Gerry North off with a good lead.

Then came John's eventful run and it had to be Hyman of Portsmouth, seventh at the time and 70 seconds behind the leaders, who was the first to realise the race was going astray, took the right course and a lead his club held to the end.
Only the wily Hyman, of the first seven, trod the correct route and, as described in the March 'BELGRAVIAN', Portsmouth were the official winners.
Gerry, Martin Hyman (Portsmouth) and Bernie Allen (Windsor & Eton) had a rare old ding dong that day – resulting in Hyman running out the winner in 23:10 with Gerry second in 23:17.
